High level: Redwood has default retention windows, but we do support customer-specific arrangements in many enterprise deals; options depend on where logs are stored (hosted vs private) and whether the data is considered customer content vs operational telemetry.

Claire — is Zenith open to an approach where we provide encrypted, write-once export bundles stored in your cloud account (we'd need a short SOW + addendum)? That typically satisfies long-term audit needs without changing our default hosted-data lifecycle.

Hi Claire, Marcus — thanks for the ping. I pulled together the current controls and options; summary below and then a proposed path forward.

Short answers:
- Standard Hosted TTLs (Redwood default):
  • API request/response logs: 90 days (operational telemetry)
  • Inference trace & KV cache artifacts: 30 days
  • Audit/authorization events (who did what): 365 days

- Customer-specific exceptions: possible, but we treat three cases differently:
  1) Hosted managed storage (Redwood-managed): we can extend retention windows up to 7 years, but this requires a legal addendum and may incur storage/operational fees. Logs remain encrypted at rest with our KMS; we provide immutable export bundles on request for audits.
  2) Dedicated / Private deployments: customers can control retention via their own infra; Redwood can provide config guidance and optional connectors to pipe logs to customer buckets with lifecycle rules.
  3) Export-only long term: we can produce an encrypted, write-once export (S3/GCS compatible) that we push to a customer-owned bucket or provide a signed, tamper-evident archive to retain for up to 7 years. This is typically the lowest-risk pattern for regulated customers.

Technical notes and constraints:
- For hosted customers with extended retention, we recommend segregating audit logs (authorization events and immutable request digests) from full API request/response payloads to limit PII exposure.
- Any export containing request/response bodies that include customer data will be treated as "customer content" and subject to the same deletion/erasure processes unless explicitly covered by an addendum.
- We can provide cryptographic checksums and a signed manifest for each export.

Evidence & controls we can supply for SIG/SOC 2:
- Redwood SOC 2 summary (redwood_soc2_summary.pdf) and auditor contact info.
- An extract of logging controls and retention policy statements mapped to SIG rows (we can produce a CSV for the highlighted rows).
- For long-tail retention requests, we add specific control objectives to the contract and provide operational runbooks for export procedures.

Proposed next steps (recommendation):
1) We prepare a short technical addendum (draft attached: proposed-data-amendment-zenith.docx) that outlines the export-only option and responsibilities.
2) Security review — Zenith review of the draft, then we finalize SOW points (storage location, encryption approach, access controls).
3) We schedule a short 30-min call to walk the procurement/legal teams through the operational steps.

If you prefer, we can also run a time-limited proof export to a test bucket to validate the process before signing.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
